test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - English Language (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question: According to Barthes, what happens when we remove the Author from our understanding of literature?

options.text: The text gains the freedom to mean different things.
The author's life becomes even more important.
Interpretation is limited to historical context.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) The text loses all meaning.***

 
 
• This **cannot be inferred** from the passage. Barthes explicitly states that refusing the Author does not mean refusing meaning.
 
 
 
• ***B) The text gains the freedom to mean different things.***
 
 
• This **can be inferred** from the passage. Barthes argues that without the Author, the text becomes open to multiple interpretations, allowing meaning to be created by the reader.
 
 
 
• ***C) The author's life becomes even more important.***
 
 
• This **cannot be inferred**. In fact, Barthes critiques the focus on the author’s life and intentions as limiting the text.
 
 
 
• ***D) Interpretation is limited to historical context.***
 
 
• This **cannot be inferred**. Barthes emphasizes that meaning is not fixed or limited but is instead an infinite play of signifiers.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2: The text gains the freedom to mean different things.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because Barthes insists meaning is not lost when the Author is removed.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because Barthes critiques the centrality of the author’s life and intentions.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because Barthes rejects limiting interpretation to historical context; meaning is created by readers.
